image_description: A close-up studio shot of an elaborate, chunky beaded necklace against a plain white background. The necklace features large, textured blue beads with intricate surface patterns, smaller translucent amber and green glass beads, and a central orange oval pendant with a floral or starburst design. Silver-toned metal wire components and clasps are visible connecting the bead clusters.

artifact_observations.location: Blue textured beads on the left cluster
artifact_observations.reasoning: The intricate lace-like texture on the large blue beads appears slightly soft and painterly upon close inspection, lacking the crisp micro-detail expected in high-resolution macro photography. It resembles AI-generated 'noise' masquerading as texture.

Some of the thin silver wires appear to merge into the beads without a clear hole or logical attachment point. The physics of how the wire loops connect to the heavy beads is ambiguous and slightly implausible.

The reflection on the orange pendant is somewhat inconsistent with the lighting direction suggested by the highlights on the surrounding blue beads, suggesting a slight compositing or generation error.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a necklace and distinguish it from other jewelry types like bracelets or earrings.
To verify that the beads are distinct objects and not melting into each other, and to check the continuity of the wire structures.
To assess the overall sharpness, lighting consistency, and detect subtle generative artifacts in the textures.
To ensure the overlapping beads and wires have correct depth ordering and do not exhibit spatial bleeding.

focus_areas: Connectivity of wire wraps to beads
Texture realism of the patterned blue beads
Logical consistency of the clasp mechanism
Lighting and reflection coherence across different materials
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'wire' elements. In AI images, thin linear structures often fail to connect logically to 3D objects. Check if the wires actually go *through* holes or just smear into the surface. Also, evaluate if the complex textures on the blue beads are coherent patterns or just high-frequency noise.
